problem: Most learning-based social navigation work targets only the local controller (vulnerable to local minima) and relies on data-hungry models (GANs, deep RL) or hand-crafted reward features (IRL). Traditional planners treat humans as obstacles.
motivation: Robots entering human environments need socially compliant navigation that is learned from few demonstrations and covers both global and local planning. Conditional Neural Processes (CNPs) can represent multimodal trajectory distributions from small datasets and can produce whole trajectories as well as reactive commands.
key_idea: Use Conditional Neural Processes trained on Social Force Model demonstrations as both the global planner (full trajectory generation) and the local planner (reactive velocity commands) in a hierarchical navigation stack.
insight: The paper qualitatively shows that a CNP generates obstacle-avoiding global paths where a 5-layer feed-forward network does not. The authors attribute this to CNPs capturing multiple modes (passing an obstacle on either side), whereas a feed-forward net interpolates between them. There is no quantitative evidence, and no ablation or statistical analysis.
method: CNP model: an encoder maps sampled trajectory points (X, γ(X), SM(X)) to latents, which are averaged into r_AVG; a query network takes X_q, γ(X_q) and r_AVG and outputs a Gaussian (μ, σ) over SM(X_q).
Demonstration data: 1000 trajectories from a Social Force Model local controller in CoppeliaSim, with random start, goal and obstacle poses, including single, multiple, static and dynamic obstacles.
Global planner CNP: X = time step, γ = (start, goal, obstacle x/y), SM = robot (x, y) position; the whole path is generated by querying all time steps at once.
Local planner CNP: X = distance to goal (x, y), γ = distance to obstacle (x, y), SM = velocity (x, y); there is no phase variable, so velocity reacts to changing obstacle positions.
Baseline: a 5-layer feed-forward neural network trained on the same 1000 trajectories, compared qualitatively on global planning.

setting.backbone: Conditional Neural Process (encoder + query MLPs, trained from scratch)
setting.training_data: 1000 simulated Social Force Model trajectories in CoppeliaSim
setting.observation: High-level state features: relative goal position and distance to obstacles (no raw sensors)
setting.action_space: Continuous 2D velocity commands (omnidirectional robot); global planner outputs position trajectories
setting.privileged: Ground-truth obstacle and goal positions and the full start/goal/obstacle configuration given as task parameters

numbers_note: No quantitative results; only qualitative figures.
results: Qualitatively, the CNP global planner produces obstacle-avoiding paths while a 5-layer feed-forward net fails. The CNP local planner avoids moving and stationary obstacles in simulation. No metrics or statistical comparison are reported.
limitations: Only preliminary qualitative results in simulation; no quantitative metrics, no strong baselines, no real-robot or human data.
Demonstrations come from SFM, which is not real human data and is itself criticized, so the learned policy may just imitate SFM.
CNPs extrapolate poorly outside the training state space, which risks collisions.
